title: Understudy role pack v1 (pack.yaml)
description: Spec 6.3. Validates pack.yaml. The files pack.yaml points at are validated against the sub-schemas in $defs (mapping, expert_steps, routine_templates, curriculum, persona, priors, task, household_generator, sites, sensitive_fields) using a ref such as pack.schema.json#/$defs/mapping. plugin_refs is accepted but never called (ROL-5).

depth.description: Returned by GET /packs. Deep packs must also carry tasks, oracle and a full expert_policy.

questions.description: Exactly the five fixed ids tools, risky, tone, pace, hours (see GET /onboarding/questions). Prompts, options and defaults differ per pack.

coverage.description: Deep packs: full. Thin packs: stub (a few checks, no oracle).

oracle.description: module:function (for example understudy_agent.sandbox_sites.oracle:score) or a path to a .py file. Deep packs only.

plugin_refs.description: Marketplace plugin references (skills as procedures, MCP servers as tools). Accepted, never called (ROL-5, D6).

oracle_note.description: Plain-language label for the oracle, for example: simplified internal rule set, illustrative, not law.

relPath.description: Relative to the pack directory. No leading slash, no '..'.

patternList.description: Case-insensitive regex patterns matched against control labels.

risk_class.description: On a risky option: the class this answer adds to the person's memory file.

patterns.description: On a risky option: label patterns added to the person's risk classes.

site.description: On a tools option: the id of the capture site (zone config) this answer enables, from tasks/sites.yaml or mapping.yaml capture_sites.

mapping.title: cogs.mapping file (mapping.yaml)
mapping.description: Same format as services/engine/understudy_engine/cogs/default_mapping.yaml, which is the source of truth for semantics. Events carry no text; the only semantic hint is meta.zone, a short enum token naming the page region the event happened in. Rules are tried in order and the first whose `match` fits wins (all match keys must fit; a list value means any-of). match keys: type, zone (meta.zone), role (target.role), source. cog: null skips the event. reformulate_as: use this cog instead when the previous mapped event was SEARCH or REFORMULATE within params.reformulate_within_s. backdate_meta: the segment starts at t minus meta[KEY] seconds. Consecutive events mapping to the same cog merge into one segment. `zones` is the pack's zone vocabulary: every match.zone and every capture zone must be listed. capture_sites tells the extension how to derive meta.zone (CSS selector to zone); the extension never reads page text for this.

capture_sites.description: Used by packs without tasks/sites.yaml (thin packs). Deep packs put capture config on each site in tasks/sites.yaml.

examples.description: Test vectors for the cog mapper: one entry in expect per event (cog id, or null when skipped).

starts.description: This event opens a new segment even if the previous segment has the same cog (a re-read is a new cog, not a longer one).

expert_steps.title: Expert policy (expert_steps.yaml)
expert_steps.description: Ordered checks forming a partial order. A check lists the cogs an expert performs for it (in order) and the checks it must come after. Any linear extension of the partial order is an allowed ordering, so independent checks may be reordered. critical checks are the ones the critic and the coach insist on; skipping one is a deficit.

question.description: A hypothesis or question for the nudge, never the answer (COA-4).

permutable.description: Checks that may occur in any order relative to each other (informational; the partial order is authoritative).

routine_templates.title: Routine templates (routines.yaml)
routine_templates.description: Templates the routine finder matches. A cluster centroid matches a template when the normalised alignment distance between cog sequences is at most match_distance.

automatable.description: False: the finder reports it but never proposes automation (too much judgement).

learning_relevant.description: True: skill gate applies, the worker's mastery of skill_cogs must be level 4 first.

params.description: Parameter slots the L1 recording replaces values with.

build_cost_runs.description: Ski rental buy cost b in units of one manual run.

curriculum.title: Curriculum (curriculum.yaml)
curriculum.description: Skills in teaching order. ladder maps each help level to the chip the overlay shows. Each skill carries a short prompt per level: a hypothesis or question, not the answer.

persona.title: Persona parameters (persona.yaml)
persona.description: Parameters for the synthetic persona and apprentice generators. The generator must use a different mechanism from the fitting models. apprentice.deficits are the planted truth for EVL-1 (which deficit was injected and what it cost).

p_at_skill0.description: Probability the deficit shows on a case at skill 0; it falls as skill rises.

price_s.description: Planted truth: mean extra seconds per case when present (direct time plus expected rework).

priors.title: Role-level priors (priors.yaml)
priors.description: Priors for partial pooling (ANA-9, ROL-6). pooling.strength is the number of pseudo-observations the role prior is worth.

task.title: Task definition (tasks/task.yaml)
task.description: Deep packs. The task the oracle scores and the completion check (AGT-4) verifies. Code, not a model, decides success: the final observation must contain every goal token. The oracle is a simplified internal rule set, illustrative, not law.

result_fields.description: Every calculator reports exactly these three fields (monthly UC amount, eligibility text, quote reference). Selectors per site are in sites.yaml.

goal_tokens.description: Placeholders such as {case_ref}, {result:ref@a}, {note_id} that the final observation must contain.

household_generator.title: Household generator config (tasks/household_generator.yaml)
household_generator.description: Describes the generator the agent-core track built (understudy_agent.sandbox_sites.households). Synthetic households only; no real people. `fields` mirrors Household.to_dict(). Cliffs are the oracle's cliff_flags names. The oracle is a simplified internal rule set, illustrative, not law.

sites.title: Sandbox sites (tasks/sites.yaml)
sites.description: Mirrors services/agent/understudy_agent/sandbox_sites/specs.py as built by the agent-core track (authoritative). Calculators a, b, c on ports 7801 to 7803 (host 127.0.0.1) and the case-note page, served by site a under /casenote. Every calculator reports exactly three fields: amount (monthly Universal Credit), status (eligibility text) and ref (quote reference). Query switches: ?variant=injected, ?layout=v2, ?glitch=503once|503always. Each calculator carries the extension's zone capture config.

served_by.description: For case_note: the calculator whose server hosts it.

submit.description: The irreversible 'Submit to claimant record' button per layout. The agent never presses it.

sensitive_fields.title: Sensitive fields list (global or pack level)
sensitive_fields.description: Same shape as packages/schema/sensitive_fields.json. Pack-level files add patterns; the effective list is the union of the global list and the pack list. Patterns are case-insensitive regexes over field name, id, label, placeholder, autocomplete and aria-label.

zoneId.description: Short enum token for a page region. Carries no page text.

selectorStr.description: A CSS selector (comma lists allowed). Used for zones only; the page text is never read.

zoneSite.description: Capture-side zone config for one site. The extension picks the config whose hosts match location.host, then derives meta.zone: for an element event the closest ancestor matching an `elements` selector (or one carrying a data-understudy-zone attribute with a vocabulary value); for document-level scroll the first matching `page` rule; for nav the first matching `nav` rule else nav_default; for tab activation the first matching `tab` rule else tab_default. Only element presence is tested, never text.

when.description: Matches when document.querySelector(when) finds an element.
